E1.evidence: Maintainer-authored issue stating the behaviour: "Its possible due to localization jumps or other behavioral servers taking control that the robot may enter a keepout zone. If the behavior isn't changed, the robot will be deadlocked in that zone." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5139 ; "this is an obvious and foreseeable deadlock condition that there needs to be some solution to get out of" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5139#issuecomment-2874998859. No reproducer or log is given; the issue is an enhancement proposal, and E1 is passed only on the maintainer's statement.

E2.evidence: The deadlock follows from the keepout filter's own policy of writing lethal cost over the zone the robot already occupies; any correct planner or controller would refuse to plan out of lethal space, so the failure does not depend on an assumption between the two units. The resolution is a new opt-in behaviour inside the filter: "If optionally enabled (default off, but on in `nav2_params.yaml`), we reduce the lethal cost to a very high but navigable cost (252) in order to allow the robot to leave on its own" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/5187 (new parameters `override_lethal_cost` and `lethal_override_cost` declared in keepout_filter.cpp). No value, frame, unit, name or timing crossing a unit boundary is wrong.

E3.evidence: If treated as a composition, PAIR (the filter's costmap output feeds the planner/controller). Not evaluated further because E2 fails.

E4.evidence: No observed instance is reported; the effect is described as foreseeable ("the robot will be deadlocked in that zone").
